title: Aleph Common Definitions
description: Shared primitives and controlled vocabularies referenced by every other Aleph schema. This file defines no root object; it exists solely to be referenced via $ref into $defs. Aleph is document-agnostic: nothing here may encode a jurisdiction, an institution, or a political position.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of the Aleph data contract this object conforms to.

data_status.description: Provenance status of the dataset. 'synthetic' means the content was generated for demonstration and describes no real statement by any real person or outlet; consumers MUST display this prominently. 'derived' means produced by the Aleph pipeline from real sources.

score_100.description: A 0-100 score. Never interpret without the accompanying polarity field.

bipolar_score.description: A -100..+100 position on a named two-poled axis. Negative means the axis's negative_label pole, positive means the positive_label pole. This is a description of where a document's identified effects fall, NOT a political-party label and NOT a left-right score.

polarity.description: How to read a 0-100 score. 'higher_is_better' means a high value indicates better epistemic practice (e.g. primary-source grounding). 'lower_is_better' means a high value indicates a problem (e.g. loaded language). 'neutral' means the score is descriptive with no implied quality ordering. Consumers MUST use this to choose colour and wording so a metric is never mis-coloured.

statement_type.description: What kind of utterance this is. Aleph must present these differently and never treat a forecast or an opinion as if it were a checkable fact. 'fact' is a verifiable assertion about what is or was. 'interpretation' is a defensible reading of facts. 'forecast' is an assertion about the future, evaluable only against its assumptions. 'opinion' is a preference. 'normative' asserts what ought to be.

verdict.description: Outcome of a speaker-blind factual evaluation. 'not_a_factual_claim' and 'forecast_conditional' exist so that opinions and predictions are never forced into a true/false frame.

evidence_strength.description: How much weight the assembled evidence can bear for a specific question. This is a property of the evidence-question pair, not of the source's prestige.

evidence_tier.description: The kind of artefact an evidence item is. Tier constrains what a source can establish; it is NOT a credibility ranking and MUST NOT be used as an authority shortcut. A primary document establishes what a text says, not whether its projections will hold. A political statement is high-relevance evidence for what an actor claimed and low-relevance for whether the claim is true.

direction.description: Sign of an estimated effect on a group or quantity.

magnitude.description: Coarse size of an estimated effect. Deliberately coarse: a false precision would overstate what the evidence supports.

causality.description: Whether an effect follows directly from a provision or through an intermediate mechanism.

readiness_state.description: Whether Aleph has collected enough context to publish verdicts. Aleph must refuse to compensate for missing evidence with model confidence.

independence.description: Whether a news item is an independent observation or a restatement of another item. Ten outlets republishing one wire story is one piece of evidence, not ten.

warm_phase.description: One of the seven fixed warm-stage phases Aleph runs before any evaluation.

id.description: Stable, human-readable, prefixed identifier. Prefixes: doc:, prov:, prop:, clm:, ev:, art:, cluster:, contra:, actor:, node:, edge:, src:, axis:, job:.

money.description: A monetary amount. Aleph never stores bare numbers for money: the currency, the scale multiplier and the reference year are all required to make a figure comparable or checkable.

year.description: Reference year for real/constant terms. Null when the source does not state one.

basis.description: e.g. 'nominal', 'constant', 'annual', 'cumulative_10y'. Null when unstated in the source.

quantity.description: A non-monetary numeric value extracted from a document, with the literal source text preserved so any transcription can be audited.

raw_text.description: Verbatim substring from the source document, before normalisation.

span.description: A located region of a source document. Character offsets are into the normalised extracted text of the given page.

text.description: The exact supporting passage, quoted verbatim. Required: an Aleph assertion with no quotable passage is not traceable.

provenance.description: Where an extracted item came from. Every proposition, provision and claim carries one. Provenance is used for authenticity and for attributing what a party officially said; it is deliberately withheld from the blind factual evaluator.

extractor.description: Identifier of the component or model version that produced this item, so results can be reproduced or invalidated.

confidence.description: Aleph separates confidence that comes from evidence from confidence reported by a language model. Consumers MUST surface evidence_confidence as the primary figure; a high model_confidence over thin evidence is meaningless and must never be presented as reassurance.

evidence_confidence.description: Derived from primary-source coverage, corroboration by independent sources, quantitative checks, temporal consistency and retrieval completeness.

model_confidence.description: Self-reported model confidence. Diagnostic only. Never the headline number.

basis.description: Named factors that raised or lowered evidence_confidence.

limiting_factor.description: The single biggest reason confidence is not higher, stated plainly for the reader.

component.description: One inspectable contributor to a composite score. No Aleph score may be published without the full list of its components: a user must always be able to open a number and see what produced it.

label.description: Plain-language description of the contributing factor, e.g. 'corporate tax rate reduction'.

weight.description: Signed contribution of this component in the score's own units.

evidence_refs.description: Ids of evidence items or provisions supporting this component.

source_ref.description: A pointer to an external source. 'tier' describes what kind of artefact it is and therefore what it can establish. There is deliberately no credibility or prestige field: Aleph must not let institutional standing substitute for evidential relevance.

uncertainty.description: An explicit statement of what remains unresolved. Aleph is required to publish these rather than round them away.

resolvable_by.description: What specific evidence would settle this, if any.
